The Markov-geometric fourth moment bound proves nonconcentration, not merely an informal inference from variance.

value.rationale: The exact sixth-degree variance of a natural classical random synchronization hitting time gives a substantive risk statistic missing from the known cubic mean. It proves an order-one relative dispersion and, with a uniform-integrability argument, genuine nonconcentration across infinitely many automata. This has clear relevance to recovery-time uncertainty and prospective scaling-limit studies, beyond routine finite computations.
